items.plain: When you yearn for good things you cannot name, and feel sad without knowing why, you are growing along with everything that grows and rising toward a larger self.
items.core_idea: Nameless longing and sorrow are signs of growth

items.plain: When my cup is empty I accept it, but when it is only half full I resent that it is not full.
items.core_idea: Partial having breeds more resentment than having nothing

items.plain: What is real in another person lies in what they cannot show you, so to understand them, listen to what they leave unsaid.
items.core_idea: Understand people by what they cannot say

items.plain: Half of what I say means nothing, but I say it so the other half can get through to you.
items.core_idea: Some words exist to carry the meaningful ones

items.plain: Having a sense of humour means seeing things in their right proportion.
items.core_idea: Humour is a sense of proportion

items.plain: My loneliness began when people praised my chatty faults and criticised my quiet virtues.
items.core_idea: Being praised for faults and blamed for virtues isolates

items.plain: A truth should always be known, but only sometimes spoken.
items.core_idea: Know truth always; speak it only sometimes

items.plain: The real part of us is quiet; the part we have picked up from outside is the part that talks.
items.core_idea: Our true self is silent, the acquired self talks

items.plain: The life in me cannot truly reach the life in you, but let us talk anyway so we do not feel alone.
items.core_idea: We talk to ease loneliness, though words cannot fully connect

items.plain: Only those who cannot speak are jealous of those who talk a lot.
items.core_idea: Only the voiceless envy the talkative

items.plain: If winter claimed to have spring in its heart, who would believe it?
items.core_idea: Claims that contradict appearances are hard to believe

items.plain: If you truly looked, you would see yourself in everything you see, and if you truly listened, you would hear your own voice in every voice.
items.core_idea: You can find yourself in everyone and everything

items.plain: Finding truth takes two people: one to say it and one to understand it.
items.core_idea: Truth needs a speaker and a listener

items.plain: Many beliefs are like a window: you see the truth through them, but they also keep you apart from it.
items.core_idea: Doctrines reveal truth yet separate us from it

items.plain: Let us play hide and seek: if you hid in my heart you would be easy to find, but if you hide inside your own shell, no one can find you.
items.core_idea: Hiding behind your defences makes you unreachable

items.plain: How noble is a sad heart that will join happy hearts in singing a happy song.
items.core_idea: It is noble to share joy while sad

items.plain: I want to walk along with everyone who is walking, not stand still and watch the procession go past.
items.core_idea: Join life rather than watch it pass

items.plain: You owe the person who serves you more than money: give them your heart, or serve them in return.
items.core_idea: Those who serve us deserve heart, not just pay

items.plain: Trees are poems the earth writes on the sky, and we cut them down to make paper so we can write down our emptiness.
items.core_idea: We destroy natural poetry to record our emptiness

items.plain: Given the choice between the power to write a poem and the joy of a poem never written, I would choose the joy, because it is the better poetry.
items.core_idea: The unwritten poem's ecstasy is better poetry

items.plain: Poetry is not stating an opinion; it is a song that comes from a painful wound or a smiling mouth.
items.core_idea: Poetry is song born of pain or joy

items.plain: If you sing about beauty, even all alone in the middle of a desert, someone will hear you.
items.core_idea: Singing of beauty always finds an audience

items.plain: Poetry is wisdom that delights the heart, and wisdom is poetry that sings in the mind.
items.core_idea: Poetry and wisdom are two faces of one thing

items.plain: We often sing lullabies to our children so that we ourselves can get to sleep.
items.core_idea: What we do for others often soothes ourselves

items.plain: A great singer is one who gives voice to what we keep silent.
items.core_idea: Great singers voice our silences

items.plain: How can you sing with a mouth full of food, or raise your hand to bless when it is full of gold?
items.core_idea: Fullness and greed block song and blessing

items.plain: People say the nightingale presses a thorn into its breast when it sings its love song; we all do the same, for how else could we sing?
items.core_idea: All true song comes from pain

items.plain: Even the most free and soaring spirit still has bodily needs it cannot escape.
items.core_idea: No spirit escapes physical needs

items.plain: A mad person is just as much a musician as you or I; only their instrument is a little out of tune.
items.core_idea: The mad share our music, slightly out of tune

items.plain: The song a mother keeps silent in her heart is sung out loud by her child.
items.core_idea: A mother's hidden song lives in her child

items.plain: Every longing is eventually fulfilled.
items.core_idea: No longing stays unfulfilled

items.plain: I have never fully agreed with my other self; the truth seems to lie somewhere between us.
items.core_idea: Truth lies between our inner selves

items.plain: Your other self always feels sorry for you, but it grows by sorrow, so all is well.
items.core_idea: Your other self grows through sorrow

items.plain: Soul and body only seem to fight in people whose souls are asleep and whose bodies are out of tune.
items.core_idea: Soul and body conflict only when out of balance

items.plain: When you reach the heart of life you will find beauty in everything, even in eyes that cannot see beauty.
items.core_idea: At life's heart, everything holds beauty

items.plain: We live only to discover beauty; everything else is a kind of waiting.
items.core_idea: Life's purpose is discovering beauty

items.plain: Plant a seed and the earth will give you a flower; dream your dream to the sky and it will bring you the one you love.
items.core_idea: What you sow and dream returns to you

items.plain: The devil died the day you were born, so now you do not have to pass through hell to meet an angel.
items.core_idea: You need not go through hell to find goodness

items.plain: If you want to possess something, you must not lay claim to it.
items.core_idea: To possess, do not claim

items.plain: When a man and a woman touch hands, they both touch the heart of eternity.
items.core_idea: A lovers' touch reaches eternity

items.plain: Love itself is the veil that hangs between two lovers.
items.core_idea: Love both joins and veils lovers

items.plain: Men who will not forgive women their small faults will never get to enjoy their great virtues.
items.core_idea: Forgive small faults to enjoy great virtues

items.plain: Love that is not made new every day turns into a habit, and then into a kind of slavery.
items.core_idea: Love must be renewed daily or it enslaves

items.plain: Lovers embrace what lies between them rather than each other.
items.core_idea: Lovers embrace their bond, not each other

items.plain: Love and doubt have never been on speaking terms with each other.
items.core_idea: Love and doubt cannot coexist

items.plain: Friendship is always a sweet duty, never a chance to gain something.
items.core_idea: Friendship is responsibility, not opportunity

items.plain: If you do not understand your friend in every kind of situation, you will never understand them.
items.core_idea: Truly knowing a friend means knowing them in all conditions

items.plain: Your finest clothes are woven by others, your tastiest meal is at another's table, your most comfortable bed is in another's house; so how can you separate yourself from other people?
items.core_idea: We cannot separate ourselves from others

items.plain: Your mind and my heart will never agree until your mind stops living in numbers and my heart stops living in fog.
items.core_idea: Mind and heart agree only when both leave extremes

items.plain: How can my heart be opened unless it is broken?
items.core_idea: A heart opens only when broken

items.plain: Only great sorrow or great joy can show who you really are.
items.core_idea: Great sorrow or joy reveals your truth

items.plain: If you want to be truly seen, you must either dance freely and openly in the sun or carry your cross.
items.core_idea: You are revealed through joy or suffering

items.plain: If nature listened to our talk of contentment, no river would seek the sea and no winter would become spring; if it listened to our talk of thrift, how many of us would even be alive?
items.core_idea: Nature ignores our talk of contentment and thrift

items.plain: When you turn your back on the sun, all you see is your own shadow.
items.core_idea: Turning from the light shows only your shadow

items.plain: You are free under the sun, the stars, and even in total darkness or with your eyes shut; but you are a slave to the one you love, and to the one who loves you.
items.core_idea: Love is the one bond that limits our freedom

items.plain: We are all beggars at the temple gate, each receiving a share of the King's gifts as he comes and goes; yet we envy one another, which belittles the King.
items.core_idea: Envying each other belittles the giver of all

items.plain: You cannot eat more than your hunger allows; the other half of the loaf belongs to someone else, and a little should be left for an unexpected guest.
items.core_idea: Take only what you need and share the rest

items.plain: Without guests, every house would be like a grave.
items.core_idea: Hospitality keeps a home alive

items.plain: I stopped my guest at the door and said, do not wipe your feet when you come in, but when you leave.
items.core_idea: A guest should take nothing away from the house

items.plain: Real generosity is not giving me what I need more than you, but giving me what you need more than I do.
items.core_idea: Generosity means giving what you yourself need

items.plain: You are truly charitable when you give while looking away, so you do not see the receiver's embarrassment.
items.core_idea: True charity spares the receiver's shame

items.plain: The difference between the richest and the poorest person is only a day of hunger and an hour of thirst.
items.core_idea: Rich and poor are separated by very little

items.plain: We often borrow from our future to pay off debts from our past.
items.core_idea: We spend our future paying for our past

items.plain: Angels and devils visit me too, but I get rid of them: I bore the angel with an old prayer, and the devil passes me by when I commit an old sin.
items.core_idea: Stale prayer and stale sin both drive visitors away

items.plain: This life is not a bad prison, though I dislike the wall between my cell and my neighbour's; yet I do not blame the guard or the Builder of the prison.
items.core_idea: Life is a fair prison, but walls divide us

items.plain: People who give you a snake when you asked for a fish may have nothing but snakes to give; for them, that is generosity.
items.core_idea: People can only give what they have

items.plain: Trickery sometimes works, but it always ends up destroying itself.
items.core_idea: Trickery always destroys itself

items.plain: You truly forgive when you forgive murderers who never shed blood, thieves who never steal, and liars who never say anything false.
items.core_idea: True forgiveness reaches hidden, unspoken wrongs

items.plain: Whoever can point to the line between good and evil can touch the hem of God's garment.
items.core_idea: Knowing good from evil brings one near God

items.plain: If your heart is a volcano, how can you expect flowers to grow in your hands?
items.core_idea: An angry heart cannot produce gentle deeds

items.plain: A strange kind of indulgence: sometimes I would let myself be wronged and cheated so I can laugh at those who think I do not know it.
items.core_idea: Letting yourself be cheated can hold secret amusement

items.plain: If someone wipes their dirty hands on your coat, let them keep the coat; they may need it again, and you surely will not.
items.core_idea: Let go of what others have soiled

items.plain: Please do not cover up your natural faults with virtues you have acquired; I would rather have the faults, since they are like my own.
items.core_idea: Honest faults are better than borrowed virtues

items.plain: How often I have claimed crimes I never committed so that another person could feel at ease with me.
items.core_idea: Admitting imagined faults can put others at ease

items.plain: Even the masks life wears hide a deeper mystery.
items.core_idea: Life's masks conceal deeper mystery

items.plain: You can judge others only by what you know of yourself; so who is guilty and who is innocent? The truly just person feels half guilty for your wrongdoing.
items.core_idea: Judge others by yourself and share their guilt

items.plain: Only when something is chasing you do you become fast.
items.core_idea: Pressure makes us swift

items.plain: O God, I have no enemies, but if I must have one, let him be as strong as I am, so that only truth wins.
items.core_idea: Wish for an equal opponent so truth prevails

items.plain: You and your enemy will get along well once you are both dead.
items.core_idea: Death ends all enmity

items.plain: A Man crucified long ago for being too loving was seen three times yesterday: asking police to spare a prostitute, drinking wine with an outcast, and fighting a promoter inside a church.
items.core_idea: Christ's love still sides with the outcast against the profiteer

items.plain: If everything people say about good and evil were true, my whole life would be one long crime.
items.core_idea: Conventional morality would condemn every life

items.plain: Pity is only half of justice.
items.core_idea: Pity falls short of justice

items.plain: The only person who has wronged me is the one whose brother I wronged first.
items.core_idea: The wrongs done to us echo the wrongs we did

items.plain: When you see someone taken to prison, think that perhaps they are escaping a narrower prison; when you see someone drunk, think that perhaps they were fleeing something even uglier.
items.core_idea: Assume hidden suffering behind others' failings

items.plain: I have often hated to protect myself, but if I were stronger I would not have needed that weapon.
items.core_idea: Hatred is a weapon of the weak

items.plain: How foolish is the person who tries to cover the hatred in their eyes with a smile.
items.core_idea: A smile cannot hide hatred in the eyes

items.plain: Only those beneath me can envy or hate me, and only those above me can praise or belittle me; since none of this happens to me, I am above and below no one.
items.core_idea: I stand equal to everyone, neither above nor below

items.plain: When you tell me you do not understand me, it is both more praise than I deserve and an insult you do not deserve.
items.core_idea: Not being understood is both praise and insult

items.plain: How petty I am when life gives me gold and I give you silver, yet I think of myself as generous.
items.core_idea: We give less than we receive yet feel generous

items.plain: When you reach the heart of life, you will find you are no higher than a criminal and no lower than a prophet.
items.core_idea: At life's heart all people are equal

items.plain: It is strange that we pity people who are slow on their feet but not those slow in mind, and the blind in eye rather than the blind in heart.
items.core_idea: We pity the wrong kinds of disability

items.plain: It is wiser for a lame person not to break their crutches over their enemy's head.
items.core_idea: Do not destroy your own support in anger

items.plain: How blind is someone who gives to you from their pocket in order to take from your heart.
items.core_idea: Giving in order to take is blindness

items.plain: Life is a procession: the slow find it too fast and drop out, and the fast find it too slow and drop out too.
items.core_idea: Both the slow and the fast leave life's procession

items.plain: If sin exists, some of us commit it backwards by following our ancestors' footsteps, and some commit it forwards by overruling our children.
items.core_idea: Sin lies in blindly following elders or dominating children

items.plain: The truly good person is one with all those who are thought of as bad.
items.core_idea: True goodness stands with the condemned

items.plain: We are all prisoners, but some of us have cells with windows and some do not.
items.core_idea: All are prisoners, some with windows

items.plain: It is strange that we all defend our wrongs more fiercely than our rights.
items.core_idea: We defend our wrongs harder than our rights

items.plain: If we all confessed our sins to one another, we would laugh at how unoriginal we are; and if we revealed our virtues, we would laugh for the same reason.
items.core_idea: Our sins and virtues are equally unoriginal

items.plain: Government is an agreement between you and me, and you and I are often wrong.
items.core_idea: Government is as fallible as the people behind it

items.plain: Crime is either another word for need or a symptom of illness.
items.core_idea: Crime springs from need or sickness

items.plain: Is there any greater fault than being aware of other people's faults?
items.core_idea: Noticing others' faults is itself a fault

items.plain: If someone laughs at you, you can pity them, but if you laugh at them you may never forgive yourself; if someone hurts you, you may forget it, but if you hurt them you will always remember.
items.core_idea: Harm we do outweighs harm done to us

items.plain: In truth, the other person is your own most sensitive self in another body.
items.core_idea: Others are your tender self in another body

items.plain: How careless you are to want others to fly with your wings when you cannot even give them a feather.
items.core_idea: You cannot make others share gifts you cannot give

items.plain: A man once ate my bread and drank my wine and left laughing at me; when he came back for more I turned him away, and the angels laughed at me.
items.core_idea: Refusing the ungrateful makes us the fools

items.plain: Hate is a dead thing, so who among you would want to be its tomb?
items.core_idea: Holding hate makes you a tomb

items.plain: The murdered person's honour is that they are not the murderer.
items.core_idea: Better to suffer wrong than to commit it

items.plain: Humanity's true voice is in its quiet heart, never in its chattering mind.
items.core_idea: Humanity speaks truly through its silent heart

items.plain: They call me mad because I will not sell my days for gold, and I call them mad because they think my days have a price.
items.core_idea: Your time is not for sale

items.plain: They lay out their gold, silver, ivory and ebony, and we lay out our hearts and spirits; yet they think they are the hosts and we the guests.
items.core_idea: Those who give their hearts are the true hosts

items.plain: I would rather be the least of people, with dreams and the will to fulfil them, than the greatest with no dreams and no desires.
items.core_idea: Better small with dreams than great without them

items.plain: The most pitiful person is the one who turns their dreams into money.
items.core_idea: Selling your dreams for money is pitiful

items.plain: We are all climbing toward what our hearts desire; if another climber steals your pack and purse and grows fat and heavy, pity him, since his climb will be harder, and help him a step, which will speed you too.
items.core_idea: Pity and help those who rob you on the climb

items.plain: You cannot judge anyone beyond what you know of them, and you know very little.
items.core_idea: Our knowledge is too small to judge others

items.plain: The truly free person is the one who patiently carries the burden of the enslaved.
items.core_idea: Freedom means patiently bearing others' burdens

items.plain: A thousand years ago my neighbour told me he hated life because it was nothing but pain; yesterday I passed a cemetery and saw life dancing on his grave.
items.core_idea: Life goes on joyfully past those who reject it

items.plain: Conflict in nature is just disorder longing to become order.
items.core_idea: Strife is disorder seeking order

items.plain: Solitude is a silent storm that breaks off our dead branches, yet it sends our living roots deeper into the living earth.
items.core_idea: Solitude clears the dead and deepens the living

items.plain: When I described the sea to a brook, it thought I was exaggerating; when I described a brook to the sea, it thought I was belittling.
items.core_idea: Each judges truth by its own scale

items.plain: How narrow is a view that values the ant's busy work above the grasshopper's singing.
items.core_idea: Song matters as much as industry

items.plain: What counts as the highest virtue here might count as the least in another world.
items.core_idea: Virtue is relative to the world we are in

items.plain: If we did not measure and weigh things, we would be as amazed by a firefly as we are by the sun.
items.core_idea: Measuring dulls our wonder

items.plain: Death is no closer to the old than to the newborn, and neither is life.
items.core_idea: Death and life are equally near at every age

items.plain: If you really must be frank, be frank in a beautiful way; otherwise stay quiet, for a man in our neighbourhood is dying.
items.core_idea: Speak honestly with grace, or keep silent

items.plain: Perhaps a funeral on earth is a wedding feast among the angels.
items.core_idea: Death here may be celebration beyond

items.plain: In truth we only ever talk to ourselves, but sometimes loudly enough for others to hear.
items.core_idea: All speech is really talking to oneself

items.plain: The obvious is something nobody sees until someone puts it simply.
items.core_idea: The obvious is unseen until simply said

items.plain: If the Milky Way were not inside me, how could I ever have seen or known it?
items.core_idea: We can know only what is already within us

items.plain: Perhaps to the sea a shell means its pearl, and perhaps to time coal means the diamond it becomes.
items.core_idea: Things are defined by what they can become

items.plain: Fame is the shadow that passion casts when it stands in the light.
items.core_idea: Fame is passion's shadow

items.plain: A root is a flower that wants nothing to do with fame.
items.core_idea: Hidden roots are humble flowers

items.plain: Beyond beauty there is neither religion nor science.
items.core_idea: Beauty underlies both religion and science

items.plain: Every great man I have known had something small in his nature, and that small thing kept him from idleness, madness or suicide.
items.core_idea: A small flaw keeps the great grounded

items.plain: The truly great person is one who would rule no one and be ruled by no one.
items.core_idea: Greatness is neither mastering nor being mastered

items.plain: Tolerance is love that has caught the disease of arrogance.
items.core_idea: Tolerance is love tainted by superiority

items.plain: A disagreement can be the quickest route between two minds.
items.core_idea: Disagreement can connect minds quickly

items.plain: I am both the flame and the dry brush, and one part of me burns up the other.
items.core_idea: We consume ourselves from within

items.plain: We are all seeking the top of the holy mountain, but would our road not be shorter if we treated the past as a map rather than a guide?
items.core_idea: Use the past as a map, not a guide

items.plain: Wisdom stops being wisdom when it becomes too proud to cry, too serious to laugh, and too self-absorbed to look beyond itself.
items.core_idea: Wisdom dies in pride, gravity and self-absorption

items.plain: If I had filled myself with everything you know, where would I have room for everything you do not know?
items.core_idea: Leave room for what is unknown

items.plain: I learned silence from talkers, tolerance from the intolerant, and kindness from the unkind; yet oddly I feel no gratitude to these teachers.
items.core_idea: We learn virtues from people who lack them

items.plain: The silence of envious people is far too loud.
items.core_idea: Envy is loud even in silence

items.plain: When you come to the end of what you should know, you will be at the beginning of what you should sense.
items.core_idea: Beyond knowledge begins intuition

items.plain: An exaggeration is a truth that has lost its temper.
items.core_idea: Exaggeration is truth in anger

items.plain: If you can see only what light shows and hear only what sound announces, then you do not truly see or hear.
items.core_idea: True perception goes beyond the senses

items.plain: You cannot laugh and be unkind at the same moment.
items.core_idea: Laughter and unkindness cannot coexist

items.plain: Closest to my heart are a king without a kingdom and a poor man who does not know how to beg.
items.core_idea: Dignity in loss and poverty moves the heart

items.plain: A modest failure is nobler than a boastful success.
items.core_idea: Humble failure beats boastful success

items.plain: Dig anywhere in the earth and you will find treasure, but you must dig with a peasant's faith.
items.core_idea: Faithful effort finds treasure anywhere

items.plain: A fox chased by twenty riders and twenty hounds said they would surely kill it, but how poor and stupid they must be, since twenty foxes on asses with twenty wolves would never bother hunting one man.
items.core_idea: Overwhelming force against the weak is foolish

items.plain: It is the mind in us that obeys the laws we make, never the spirit.
items.core_idea: Man-made laws bind the mind, not the spirit

items.plain: I am a traveller and a navigator, and every day I discover a new region in my own soul.
items.core_idea: Each day reveals new regions of the soul

items.plain: A woman protested that of course the war was righteous, because her son died in it.
items.core_idea: Grief makes us call our losses righteous

items.plain: I told Life I wanted to hear Death speak, and Life simply raised her voice a little and said that I was hearing him now.
items.core_idea: Death speaks through life itself

items.plain: When you have solved every mystery of life, you long for death, since it is just one more mystery of life.
items.core_idea: Death is life's final mystery

items.plain: Birth and death are the two noblest acts of courage.
items.core_idea: Birth and death are supreme acts of bravery

items.plain: My friend, we will stay strangers to life, to each other and to ourselves until you speak and I listen as if your voice were mine, and I stand before you as if before a mirror.
items.core_idea: We become known only by seeing ourselves in each other

fix.display_text: My friend, you and I shall remain strangers unto life, And unto one another, and each unto himself, Until the day when you shall speak and I shall listen Deeming your voice my own voice; And when I shall stand before you Thinking myself standing before a mirror.

items.plain: People tell me that knowing myself would let me know everyone; I reply that only by seeking everyone will I know myself.
items.core_idea: Self-knowledge comes through seeking others

items.plain: Each person is two people: one awake in the dark, the other asleep in the light.
items.core_idea: We are awake in darkness and asleep in light
